recommendation: Keep the audit commit. Do not change the current returned-in wording back to persisted-to because FHIR-23565 is a later published clarification of the same requirement and covers non-persisted expansion results.
issue_request: FHIR-22664 was Published/Persuasive with Modification for R5 by Vocabulary and asked for guidance on the ValueSet expansion and ValueSet $expand pages clarifying what ValueSet.version (and status) mean when a ValueSet instance contains only expansion without compose.
initial_application: Commit 9fca6ca36fefa544491b1efc7fdb1530333ed78b, an R5/VSD profile batch explicitly listing FHIR-22664, added the status/version rule to source/valueset/valueset-notes.xml and source/valueset/operationdefinition-ValueSet-expand.xml using the Jira resolution's persisted-to wording.
additional_context: Later same-family issue FHIR-23565 was Published/Persuasive with Modification for R5 and clarified that persistence is not the controlling distinction. Its accepted wording says the values SHALL be returned in the expansion ValueSet, and reconciliation commit b04f6401acc7d52bf98b74b85afa2d8d3f2dca23 aligned the remaining stale $expand operation footer. Vocab/VSDP Confluence records approve FHIR-22664 and show the FHIR-23565 discussion treating the returned-in statement as satisfying the original request.
reconciliation: No source change was made. source/valueset/valueset-notes.xml and source/valueset/operationdefinition-ValueSet-expand.xml both now state that, when available, ValueSet.status and ValueSet.version from the ValueSet resource instance containing the definition SHALL be returned in the ValueSet resource instance containing the expansion.

related_jiras.note: Later Published/Persuasive with Modification ValueSet issue that refined the same expansion status/version requirement from persistence-focused wording to returned-in wording; already represented on the combined branch.
